issue_context.title: No enum constant org.duckdb.DuckDBColumnType.TIME WITH TIME ZONE when querying DatabaseMetaData::getColumns
issue_context.body:
### What happens?

The `TIME WITH TIME ZONE` data type isn't supported by the JDBC driver's `DatabaseMetaData` implementation.

### To Reproduce

```java
try (Statement s = connection.createStatement()) {
    try {
        s.executeUpdate("create table t (i time with time zone)");
        connection.getMetaData().getColumns(null, "%", "t", "i");
    }
    finally {
        s.executeUpdate("drop table t");
    }
}
```

This produces:

```
Exception in thread "main" java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: No enum constant org.duckdb.DuckDBColumnType.TIME WITH TIME ZONE
	at java.base/java.lang.Enum.valueOf(Enum.java:273)
	at org.duckdb.DuckDBColumnType.valueOf(DuckDBColumnType.java:3)
	at org.duckdb.DuckDBResultSetMetaData.TypeNameToType(DuckDBResultSetMetaData.java:58)
	at org.duckdb.DuckDBDatabaseMetaData.getColumns(DuckDBDatabaseMetaData.java:827)
	at org.jooq.testscripts.JDBC.main(JDBC.java:46)
```

### OS:

Microsoft Windows [Version 10.0.22621.1555]

### DuckDB Version:

v0.7.1

### DuckDB Client:

JDBC

### Full Name:

Lukas Eder

### Affiliation:

Data Geekery / jOOQ

### Have you tried this on the latest `master` branch?

- [X] I agree

### Have you tried the steps to reproduce? Do they include all relevant data and configuration? Does the issue you report still appear there?

- [X] I agree
comments: I would guess this is probably due to the underscores instead of spaces in the enum lookup?

There's no enum value for the type:
https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/master/tools/jdbc/src/main/java/org/duckdb/DuckDBColumnType.java

And `DuckDBResultSetMetaData::TypeNameToType` doesn't map it either:
https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/master/tools/jdbc/src/main/java/org/duckdb/DuckDBResultSetMetaData.java#L46

It does correctly handle `TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE`

I just realised that

1. The version on `master` will intercept the exception and return `UNKNOWN`
2. The type isn't documented: https://duckdb.org/docs/sql/data_types/timestamp, yet it's not being rejected by the `CREATE TABLE` statement either.

This shows that it seems to be accepted by the database:

```sql
create table t (i time with time zone);

select *
from duckdb_columns()
where table_name = 't';
```

Possibly some lacking documentation?
Yeah I just noticed that as well, I guess it isn't commonly used, so this hasn't come up before

review_comments:
Is the standard `TIME` class also missing? Can we add that as well?

It also doesn't matter but technically `time` should use `dtime_t` instead of `timestamp_t` (they are the same byte size so it should have no impact in this case).

Unrelated to this PR but I wonder if the non-microsecond timestamp types are handled correctly. It seems like they use the exact same code path as the regular timestamps - which will likely result in incorrect conversions. The types are almost never used outside of conversions from specific formats (e.g. Arrow) so it is not that unthinkable that these have not been correctly tested in the JDBC client.

Perhaps it makes sense to add the `test_all_types` test to the JDBC client as well?
